$description: Machine-readable schema for bioinformatics file comparison strategies. Used by StrategyRecommender to guide LLM strategy and parameter selection.

exact.when_to_use: Task requires identical sequences (e.g., genome assembly reproducibility, format conversion). Same input always produces same output.

parameters.name: by_name
parameters.description: If true, match sequences by ID; if false, match by sequence content

parameters.name: ignore_case
parameters.description: Uppercase sequences before comparison

parameters.name: single_line
parameters.description: If true, sequences spanning multiple lines in the candidate are excluded and counted as absent — use when the task requires single-line FASTA output (e.g., multiline-to-single-line conversion). Leave false (default) for all other FASTA tasks: BioPython normalizes line breaks during loading, so multiline sequences compare identically to single-line ones and no penalty is applied.

approximate.when_to_use: Task may produce similar but not identical sequences (e.g., assembly polishing, consensus calling, minor indels expected). Uses Smith-Waterman local alignment.

parameters.name: by_name
parameters.description: If true, match by sequence ID; if false, greedy content-based matching

parameters.name: ignore_case
parameters.description: Uppercase sequences before comparison

parameters.name: single_line
parameters.description: If true, sequences spanning multiple lines in the candidate are excluded and counted as absent — use when the task requires single-line FASTA output (e.g., multiline-to-single-line conversion). Leave false (default) for all other FASTA tasks: BioPython normalizes line breaks during loading, so multiline sequences compare identically to single-line ones and no penalty is applied.

summary.when_to_use: Sequence-level comparison is impractical (large assemblies, metagenomics). Only overall composition needs to match. Compares k-mer distributions and length distributions.

parameters.name: k
parameters.description: K-mer size for frequency distribution comparison

parameters.name: num_bins
parameters.description: Number of histogram bins for length distribution

parameters.name: ignore_case
parameters.description: Uppercase sequences before k-mer extraction

exact.when_to_use: Task requires identical read output (e.g., reproducibility of trimming or filtering). Read IDs, sequences, and quality scores must all match.

approximate.when_to_use: Different trimming tools may trim reads slightly differently at ends. Allows positional tolerance and Phred score tolerance. Do NOT use for random subsampling — use 'summary' instead.

parameters.name: trim_tolerance
parameters.description: Maximum bases allowed to differ at sequence ends (trimming tolerance)

parameters.name: quality_tolerance
parameters.description: Maximum allowed difference in Phred quality scores per base

summary.when_to_use: Overall QC comparison without read-level alignment. Compares read counts, length distributions, and k-mer frequency distributions.

parameters.name: k
parameters.description: K-mer size for frequency distribution comparison

parameters.name: num_bins
parameters.description: Number of histogram bins for length distribution

exact.when_to_use: RARELY appropriate. Only when the task explicitly requires a bit-identical table: same column names, same column order, same row order, exact values. Any structural difference (reordering, casing, rounding) will score 0.0 even for correct outputs. Prefer 'approximate' for all typical bioinformatics table tasks.

parameters.name: question
parameters.default: Compare two tabular data files for equivalence
parameters.description: Task context for LLM comparison planning

approximate.when_to_use: DEFAULT for all table files. Handles column reordering, row reordering, case differences, and minor numeric rounding via 3-phase LLM-planned alignment. Even 'deterministic' tasks (filtering, normalization, DEG analysis) routinely produce tables with structural differences that are not errors.

parameters.name: question
parameters.default: Compare two tabular data files for equivalence
parameters.description: Task context passed to LLM for alignment planning

summary.when_to_use: Very large tables where LLM calls are cost-prohibitive, or when only aggregate statistics need to match (task produces a statistical summary, not data records). No LLM calls.

semantic.when_to_use: Table content requires semantic understanding beyond structural alignment (e.g., different representations of the same biological finding). Sends data preview to LLM for holistic judgment.

parameters.name: question
parameters.default: Compare two tabular data files for equivalence
parameters.description: Task context for LLM holistic judgment

parameters.name: max_rows
parameters.description: Maximum rows from each file to include in LLM preview

exact.when_to_use: Task requires bit-identical alignment output (e.g., deterministic aligner reproducibility check). All records must be identical.

approximate.when_to_use: Different aligners or parameter sets may place reads slightly differently. Matches reads by QNAME, checks mapping concordance within 10bp positional window.

parameters.name: min_mapq
parameters.description: Minimum MAPQ score; reads below threshold are excluded from comparison

parameters.name: overlap_threshold
parameters.description: Minimum fractional CIGAR overlap required for a read pair to be concordant

parameters.name: chunk_size
parameters.description: Number of reads processed per chunk for memory efficiency

summary.when_to_use: DEFAULT. Quick alignment quality agreement check via flagstat statistics and MAPQ distribution. Good for most alignment tasks without read-level comparison.

coverage.when_to_use: Task is about coverage uniformity rather than individual read placement (e.g., target enrichment uniformity, whole-genome coverage). Uses samtools depth.

parameters.name: depth0_similarity
parameters.description: Similarity score assigned when both files have depth 0 at a position. null = exclude such positions from the mean.

variant.when_to_use: Goal is functional equivalence at the variant level — do both alignments produce the same variant calls? Calls variants via bcftools mpileup+call, then delegates to VCFHandler.

parameters.name: ref_fasta
parameters.description: Path to reference FASTA file required by bcftools mpileup

parameters.name: vcf_strategy
parameters.description: VCF comparison strategy to apply after variant calling

functional.when_to_use: DEFAULT. Verifies the index provides the same per-chromosome read counts and lengths via samtools idxstats. Auto-discovers the indexed BAM/CRAM file from index path if not provided.

parameters.name: indexed_file
parameters.description: Path to the BAM/CRAM file indexed by both index files. Auto-discovered from index paths if omitted.

summary.when_to_use: Quick sanity check comparing only file sizes. Use when the indexed BAM/CRAM file is unavailable.

parameters.name: indexed_file
parameters.description: Path to the indexed BAM/CRAM file (optional for summary strategy)

exact.when_to_use: Task requires identical variant call output — same position, REF/ALT alleles, QUAL, FILTER, and annotation fields in the same order.

approximate.when_to_use: Different variant callers may report the same variant at slightly different positions or with different representations. Matches variants within a position window.

parameters.name: position_window
parameters.description: Maximum allowed position difference in base pairs for variant matching

parameters.name: require_allele_match
parameters.description: If true, REF/ALT alleles must match exactly in addition to position

summary.when_to_use: DEFAULT. Quick assessment of variant calling agreement via precision, recall, and F1 on variant overlap. Good default for most variant calling benchmarks.

exact.when_to_use: Task requires identical interval output — same coordinates and scores in the same order.

parameters.name: coord_only
parameters.description: If true, compare only core 3 columns (chrom, start, end); ignore score and other columns

parameters.name: ignore_order
parameters.description: If true, sort regions before comparing (order-invariant exact match)

parameters.name: merge_overlap
parameters.description: If true, merge overlapping intervals before comparing

approximate.when_to_use: DEFAULT. Peak callers or interval tools may produce slightly different boundaries for the same features. Calculates Jaccard similarity with positional tolerance.

parameters.name: tolerance
parameters.description: Positional tolerance in base pairs — extends alt intervals before overlap check

parameters.name: overlap_threshold
parameters.description: Minimum overlap fraction relative to reference region for a match to count

parameters.name: coord_only
parameters.description: If true, compare only core 3 columns (chrom, start, end)

parameters.name: ignore_order
parameters.description: If true, sort regions before comparing

parameters.name: merge_overlap
parameters.description: If true, merge overlapping intervals before comparing

overlap.when_to_use: Care about total genomic coverage agreement rather than individual region matching. Merges intervals first, then calculates base-level Jaccard overlap.

parameters.name: coord_only
parameters.description: If true, compare only core 3 columns (chrom, start, end)

parameters.name: merge_overlap
parameters.description: If true, merge overlapping intervals before base-level comparison

parameters.name: ignore_order
parameters.description: If true, sort regions before comparing

correlation.when_to_use: BED files have quantitative score columns (e.g., signal intensity, ChIP-seq enrichment) and you want to compare score patterns on overlapping regions.

parameters.name: overlap_threshold
parameters.description: Minimum overlap fraction for two regions to be considered matched

parameters.name: correlation_method
parameters.description: Correlation method for score comparison

summary.when_to_use: Quick aggregate comparison of region counts, length distributions, and score distributions. No region-level alignment.

parameters.name: num_bins
parameters.description: Number of bins for value distribution histogram

exact.when_to_use: Task requires identical signal track output — all genomic position values must match exactly.

parameters.name: max_positions
parameters.description: Maximum positions sampled per chromosome. null = all positions.

approximate.when_to_use: Signal values may differ slightly due to normalization or processing differences. Compares per-position values within relative tolerance.

parameters.name: tolerance
parameters.description: Relative tolerance for value comparison (1 = 100% relative difference allowed)

parameters.name: max_positions
parameters.description: Maximum positions sampled per chromosome. null = all positions.

correlation.when_to_use: Care about signal patterns rather than absolute values (e.g., comparing enrichment profiles). Scale-invariant: same pattern with different magnitudes scores high.

parameters.name: correlation_method
parameters.description: Correlation method for signal comparison

parameters.name: max_positions
parameters.description: Maximum positions sampled per chromosome. null = all positions.

summary.when_to_use: DEFAULT. Quick assessment of signal distribution agreement using Hellinger distance on per-chromosome value histograms. Good default for most signal track comparisons.

parameters.name: max_positions
parameters.description: Maximum positions sampled per chromosome. null = all positions.

parameters.name: num_bins
parameters.description: Number of histogram bins for value distribution comparison

exact.when_to_use: Task requires identical annotation output — all feature fields (seqid, source, featuretype, start, end, score, strand, frame, attributes) must match.

approximate.when_to_use: Annotation tools may produce slightly different feature boundaries. Counts overlapping features by seqid and featuretype with positional tolerance.

parameters.name: tolerance
parameters.description: Positional tolerance in base pairs to extend intervals when matching features

parameters.name: overlap_threshold
parameters.description: Minimum overlap ratio relative to reference feature length for a match to count

summary.when_to_use: DEFAULT. Quick assessment of annotation agreement via feature counts, type distributions, and length distributions. No feature-level matching.

exact.when_to_use: DEFAULT. Index must be identical — same sequence names, lengths, offsets, line widths (e.g., same FASTA indexed with same tool).

approximate.when_to_use: Index may differ slightly (e.g., different line widths but same sequences). Compares length values using Relative Absolute Error.

parameters.name: tolerance
parameters.description: RAE threshold for length values; 0.0 means any difference fails

parameters.name: max_rae
parameters.description: Maximum RAE assigned to sequences missing in the alternative index

summary.when_to_use: Quick check that indexes reference sequences of similar count and length distribution. No sequence-level matching.

parameters.name: num_bins
parameters.description: Number of histogram bins for sequence length distribution comparison

functional.when_to_use: DEFAULT. Verifies index covers the same genomic contigs/chromosomes and lengths. Auto-discovers the indexed file from index path if not provided.

parameters.name: indexed_file
parameters.description: Path to the indexed file (VCF/BCF/BED/etc.). Auto-discovered from index path if omitted (e.g., file.vcf.gz.tbi → file.vcf.gz).

summary.when_to_use: Quick sanity check comparing only file sizes. Use when the indexed file is unavailable.

parameters.name: indexed_file
parameters.description: Path to the indexed file (optional for summary strategy)

exact.when_to_use: DEFAULT. Task requires identical protein structure output — chains must have identical sequences AND near-zero RMSD (< 0.001 Å).

parameters.name: by_name
parameters.description: If true, match chains by chain ID; if false, match chains by sequence content

approximate.when_to_use: Structure prediction or modeling may produce similar but not identical structures. Combines sequence alignment similarity and RMSD-based structural similarity.

parameters.name: by_name
parameters.description: If true, match chains by chain ID; if false, match by sequence content

parameters.name: sequence_weight
parameters.description: Weight for sequence similarity component (must sum to 1.0 with structure_weight)

parameters.name: structure_weight
parameters.description: Weight for structural (RMSD) similarity component

parameters.name: rmsd_threshold
parameters.description: RMSD threshold in Ångströms for exponential decay similarity: sim = exp(-RMSD / threshold)

summary.when_to_use: Quick comparison of protein structure properties (chain count, residue count, atom count, chain length distribution) without alignment.

parameters.name: num_bins
parameters.description: Number of histogram bins for chain length distribution comparison

exact.when_to_use: Task requires identical R object output — shape, dimension names, and all values must match within tolerance. Seurat/SCE objects are delegated to AnnData exact comparison.

parameters.name: tolerance
parameters.description: Floating-point tolerance for numeric comparisons

approximate.when_to_use: R outputs may differ in precision or have minor differences but represent equivalent results. Aligns to common rows/columns and compares element-wise.

parameters.name: tolerance
parameters.description: Numeric tolerance for element-wise comparison

summary.when_to_use: DEFAULT. Quick comparison of R object types, dimensions, and statistical properties. No element-level alignment. Seurat/SCE delegates to AnnData summary.

exact.when_to_use: Task requires identical single-cell data output — shape, obs/var index, count matrix, and metadata must all match within float tolerance.

parameters.name: tolerance
parameters.description: Floating-point tolerance for matrix comparison

parameters.name: layer
parameters.description: Layer name to compare (e.g., 'counts', 'normalized'). null = use X matrix.

approximate.when_to_use: Matrices may differ in precision or subsetting but represent equivalent data. Aligns to common obs/var, then compares element-wise within tolerance.

parameters.name: tolerance
parameters.description: Numeric tolerance for element-wise matrix comparison

parameters.name: layer
parameters.description: Layer name to compare. null = use X matrix.

parameters.name: cluster_col
parameters.description: Cluster column name in obs metadata. null = auto-detect (tries 'leiden', 'louvain', etc.).

summary.when_to_use: DEFAULT. Standard comparison for single-cell outputs. Checks cell/gene counts, cluster assignment agreement (ARI), and embedding correlation. Good default for clustering and dimensionality reduction tasks.

parameters.name: reduction
parameters.description: Embedding key in obsm to compare (e.g., 'X_umap', 'X_pca')

parameters.name: cluster_col
parameters.description: Cluster column name in obs. null = auto-detect.

exact.when_to_use: Task produces deterministic text output that should be identical line-by-line.

parameters.name: ignore_whitespace
parameters.description: If true, remove all whitespace before comparing

parameters.name: ignore_case
parameters.description: If true, convert to lowercase before comparing

approximate.when_to_use: Text may have insertions, deletions, or reordering of lines but similar content. Uses difflib.SequenceMatcher.

parameters.name: compare_by
parameters.description: 'line' for line-by-line comparison; 'text' for full character-level comparison

parameters.name: ignore_whitespace
parameters.description: If true, normalize whitespace before comparing

parameters.name: ignore_case
parameters.description: If true, convert to lowercase before comparing

semantic.when_to_use: DEFAULT. Text reports, logs, or summaries that may express the same findings differently. LLM checks if the alternative text contains all key information from the reference.

parameters.name: question
parameters.description: Optional task context for the LLM comparison

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: LLM model to use for semantic comparison

summary.when_to_use: Quick structural comparison of text length and volume (line/word/character counts) without content analysis.

numeric.when_to_use: Both files contain one or more raw numeric values (scalars, small lists). Uses relative absolute error (RAE) to compute similarity. Suitable for outputs like p-values, fold-changes, counts, or any text file whose content is purely numeric.

semantic.when_to_use: Only available strategy. LLM visually assesses whether images show the same biological information (e.g., similar plots with different styling).

parameters.name: question
parameters.description: Optional task context for the LLM visual comparison

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: LLM model to use for visual comparison

semantic.when_to_use: Only available strategy. LLM assesses functional equivalence of code logic — whether scripts implement the same computational steps.

parameters.name: question
parameters.description: Optional task context for the LLM code equivalence assessment

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: LLM model to use for code comparison

exact.when_to_use: DEFAULT. Task produces a directory (e.g., genome index, pipeline output folder) that should be exactly reproducible. All files must be present and byte-identical.

parameters.name: ignore_patterns
parameters.description: List of filename patterns to exclude (e.g., ['.git', '__pycache__', '*.log'])

approximate.when_to_use: Directory contents may differ slightly (e.g., log files, metadata files) but core outputs should match. Files are matched by relative path; concordant if content similarity ≥ threshold.

parameters.name: ignore_patterns
parameters.description: List of filename patterns to exclude

parameters.name: content_threshold
parameters.description: Minimum content similarity for a file pair to be considered concordant

summary.when_to_use: Quick structural comparison of directory contents — file count, total size, extension distribution. No per-file content comparison.

parameters.name: ignore_patterns
parameters.description: List of filename patterns to exclude

exact.when_to_use: Task requires identical mass spectrometry XML output — element-by-element XML tree comparison.

parameters.name: tolerance
parameters.description: Relative tolerance for numeric value comparisons within XML elements

approximate.when_to_use: Different tools or parameters may produce slightly different mass spec results. Matches features/spectra by proximity (RT, m/z) and compares numeric values within tolerance.

parameters.name: tolerance
parameters.description: Relative tolerance for numeric comparisons (intensity, charge, score)

parameters.name: rt_tolerance
parameters.description: Retention time matching window in seconds for feature/spectrum matching

parameters.name: mz_tolerance
parameters.description: m/z matching window in Daltons for feature matching

summary.when_to_use: DEFAULT. Quick comparison of mass spec output profiles via element counts, type distributions, and numeric value distributions. Good default for most mass spec tasks.
